subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this canonical readiness-condition model, plugin readiness provider API, and standard hosting-profile configuration as core, release-tested contracts?
rationale: The RFC creates permanent cross-cutting API, configuration, runtime, and support semantics whose scope and ownership cannot be approved from document correctness alone.

options.title: Continue integrated RFC
options.body: Review the condition model, provider API, and standard profiles together while requiring explicit compatibility and release-conformance commitments.

options.title: Stage the contracts
options.body: Accept normalization of existing Gateway readiness first and defer plugin providers or non-local profiles to follow-up RFCs.

options.title: Keep hosting external
options.body: Decline the new core contracts and leave higher-level hosting readiness to downstream hosts and plugins.

recommendation.title: Continue integrated RFC
recommendation.body: Review the condition model, provider API, and standard profiles together while requiring explicit compatibility and release-conformance commitments.

likelyOwner.reason: Their repository history introduced the formal RFC acceptance process, while runtime-domain ownership can be added during discussion.
